text:
sara: Heads-up: I'm experimenting with a micro-slab allocator for Dedicated pools. Goal: reduce fragmentation and increase tenant density without changing the operator's physical lease model. Need quick feedback on API surface, safety, and rollout.

devin: Quick question: how is this different from fractional-token ideas we've kicked around?

sara: It's similar in spirit but implemented as a local proxy/allocator that packs fractional "slabs" into full GPU leases. The operator still only creates/destroys physical leases. Allocator handles packing, merges, and soft eviction.

mike: Main risks I see: 1) shared GPU memory and KV cache contamination across slabs; 2) unpredictable latency if many slabs contend on one card. How do we isolate and signal those conditions?

sara: Plan: logical namespaces per slab for KV to avoid keyspace collisions, and per-slab memory quotas enforced by the runtime adapter. If contention rises allocator will stop admitting new slabs onto that physical lease and return a short throttle window.

anya: Operator boundary: keep it minimal. Operator gets an "intent document" describing desired physical capacity (n GPUs, labels, generation). Allocator reconciles slab packing and periodically reconciles its needs with the operator. No per-slab ops to operator.

devin: Nice. What about failure scenarios: allocator restart or crash? We can't lose slab state or double-allocate.

sara: We'll persist slab manifests in etcd. Allocator uses lease epochs and CAS on physical-lease versions to avoid races during split/merge. On restart it rebuilds packing from durable manifests and asks operator for current physical leases.

mike: Eviction semantics? If allocator overcommits or an OOM happens mid-request, what's the fallback?

sara: Eviction order: 1) soft reclaim idle slabs (return to pool), 2) cooperative shrink (ask tenant to release lower-QoS slabs), 3) operator-scale (request new physical leases) or migrate active slabs off the node. We'll surface explicit admit responses with fields: admitted:true/false, lease_id, slab_count, throttle_until, eviction_policy_hint.

anya: Observability: we need slab pack ratio, slab churn rate, per-physical contention score, per-tenant tail-latency, and reconcile-failure counts. Add traces linking request->allocator->operator->node.

devin: Rollout plan: start in a single region with a small canary tenant list. Provide a runtime flag so we can route a percentage of traffic to allocator path. Must support full fallback to baseline admission (no allocator).

sara: Exactly. We'll implement routing policy: allocator-preferred with fallback. Start at zero overcommit (1:1 slab capacity to physical capacity), then enable conservative overcommit after stability window.

mike: Billing mapping is tricky. Tenants will see fractional usage but want predictable invoices. Suggest the allocator expose a usage aggregation endpoint that rounds up to nearest minute and ties slab-minute to GPU-minute equivalent with clear rules.

sara: We'll produce /usage reports and also feed usage into billing pipeline. Docs will show rounding and minimum billing granularity.

anya: Ops tooling: add a drain CLI that moves slabs off a physical lease (force migrate) and a debug endpoint that prints packing layout. Also a metric alert when physical pack density exceeds configured threshold.

sara: For safety: allocator will be conservative by default, require opt-in by tenant and add a quota cap per-tenant so a single tenant can't saturate multiple slabs on the same physical.

devin: One more: how do we handle heterogeneous hardware and model compatibility (tensor cores, quantized kernels)?

sara: Allocator will maintain a compatibility matrix for physical leases (labels for arch, mem, quant-friendly) and only place slabs with compatible runtimes on matching nodes. Incompatible requests will be admitted to a different path or rejected.

mike: Sounds reasonable. Add an alert for packing decisions that violate compatibility. Also recommend a nightly defragment job to proactively merge small slabs into fewer physical leases when utilization drops.

ops-bot: canary cluster deployment initiated for micro-slab-allocator in eu-central-1  build#4892

sara: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC with API examples (POST /alloc/admit, POST /alloc/release, GET /alloc/usage), operator intent schema, and a canary checklist. Schedule follow-up to review the RFC.

anya: I'll add dashboards and an initial SLO: 95% admits < 50ms.

mike: I'll draft a one-pager on eviction and OOM drills.

devin: Great. Appreciate the quick sync.

sara: Thanks all. We'll iterate after RFC. End of thread.
